title: Schools Tackling Impact of Posting Group Banding to Promote Inclusivity and Friendships
what_it_is: Schools Tackling Impact of Posting Group Banding to Promote Inclusivity and Friendships

sections.label: Posting Groups and Full SBB
sections.summary: Posting Groups guide Secondary 1 entry, and Full SBB places students in mixed form classes with common subjects and teacher support.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Jasmin Lau) (for the Minister for Education)
sentences.text: Posting Groups (PGs) are used to facilitate students' entry into secondary schools and guide students to take subjects at appropriate levels at the start of Secondary 1.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Jasmin Lau) (for the Minister for Education)
sentences.text: Students admitted through different PGs may take subjects at similar levels, depending on their individual strengths.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Jasmin Lau) (for the Minister for Education)
sentences.text: Under our Full Subject-Based Banding (Full SBB), our secondary school students are placed in mixed form classes, where they spend around a third of their curriculum time taking common subjects, such as Art and Character Citizenship Education with peers from different subject levels and combinations.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Jasmin Lau) (for the Minister for Education)
sentences.text: This approach gives students more opportunities than under the previous streaming system to interact with and to learn with classmates with different strengths and interests.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Jasmin Lau) (for the Minister for Education)
sentences.text: The Ministry of Education (MOE) is mindful of potential challenges that some students may face, including with social interactions in a more diverse classroom setting.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Jasmin Lau) (for the Minister for Education)
sentences.text: And this is why we provide teachers with resources and professional development opportunities to support students in Full SBB schools.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Jasmin Lau) (for the Minister for Education)
sentences.text: For example, our teachers use termly check-in surveys to understand their students' interests, emotional well-being and peer support networks, which in turn, help them to foster a positive classroom culture.

sections.label: Emotional well-being in mixed classes
sections.summary: Teachers receive tools and strategies, including termly check-ins and peer support network mapping, to monitor students' emotional well-being.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jasmin Lau
sentences.text: One of the concerns for mixed form classes is the emotional well-being and support systems for all of our students, because they come from different backgrounds and may have different life experiences.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jasmin Lau
sentences.text: So, a lot of our focus in terms of supporting our teachers is in providing them with tools and strategies to understand and monitor our students' emotional well-being.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jasmin Lau
sentences.text: As I mentioned, the termly check-ins do focus on their emotional well-being and peer support systems, and we also provide teachers with tools to help map out their students' peer support networks.
